Prince Sher Singh's claim to the throne was contested by the widows of Kharak Singh and Nan Nihal Singh on behalf of the expected issue of the latter. Sher Singh, not feeling quite strong at the time, yielded to the proposal that Chand Kaur should exercise the supreme power as regent till the widow of Nau Nihal Singh was delivered of a son. But this was obviously to bide kb time, for, as soon as he was able to strengthen his resources, Sher Singh made a bid for the throne and in January 1841 besieged the fort of Lahore with an overwhelming army. Rani Chand Kaur and his daughter-in-law were granted a suitable pension ; and after a short time the former was beaten to death by her maid servants, presumably by the order of the Maharaja. (i) Mai.
